claims.text: Rare CHD types make large training cohorts difficult to acquire, while prior cardiac generative approaches primarily model normal topology and do not readily capture CHD topological variations.

SDF4CHD disentangles CHD type and patient-specific shape using diagnosis-conditioned implicit anatomical templates, a deformation module, and a correction module for additional patient-specific topological variations.
The shape module uses neural ordinary differential equations to learn invertible deformations, with a spatial latent code of 4×4×4×27.
In practice, training used occupancy values rather than signed distances; anatomical boundaries were represented by the 0.5-level set.

The study used imageCHD CT data and diagnosis labels with segmentations of seven cardiac structures, manually processed under radiology expert supervision; the reported splits contained 67 training, 8 validation, and 34 testing patients.
The six modeled CHD types were ASD, VSD, DORV, pulmonary atresia, tetralogy of Fallot, and d-transposition of the great arteries.

In blinded manual assessment of 50 randomly generated cases per method, input diagnoses disagreed with diagnoses inferred from generated anatomy in 3 SDF4CHD cases and 48 CDeepSDF cases; most SDF4CHD discrepancies involved distinguishing DORV from ToF.

Across 30 generated anatomies per CHD type, SDF4CHD had higher mean shape plausibility scores than separate networks trained per type; plausibility was measured as maximum Dice similarity to training anatomies.
For unseen anatomy reconstruction, whole-heart Dice was 86.3 ± 2.7 without correction and 88.8 ± 2.0 with correction; CDeepSDF and DeepSDF each achieved 88.8 ± 2.7.

Adding 420 synthetic images to 67 real training images improved test whole-heart Dice from 84.7 ± 6.0 to 86.3 ± 5.3 for 3D UNet and from 82.1 ± 7.1 to 84.0 ± 6.3 for 2D UNet; both improvements were reported as significant.
With synthetic augmentation, 3D UNet median VSD diameter percentage error decreased from 54% to 38%, and median area percentage error decreased from 72% to 59%.
The method failed to reconstruct an apical VSD in a test case with two VSDs because its learned templates contained only subaortic VSDs; the correction network also missed the apical defect.
The shared Gaussian shape prior across CHD types is a simplifying assumption; patient-specific shape distributions may differ by type and are difficult to capture with few examples.
Higher-resolution latent shape codes improved reconstruction but produced non-physiological distortions during synthetic generation.
The predicted diffeomorphic mapping does not guarantee strictly positive mesh-element Jacobians, despite reducing surface-intersection artifacts.
SDF4CHD and the baselines struggled to represent smaller vessel branches; generative modeling of vessel-connection variations was not extensively explored.

The contribution is a type-controlled cardiac generative representation combining smooth implicit fields and diffeomorphic deformations, with demonstrated applications to synthetic image-segmentation pairs and computational-simulation meshes.
